question: How many singers, each as loud as a soloist and not in lockstep, does it take to sound twice as loud?
move: When perception runs on ratios, doubling the effect costs far more than doubling the effort.
trap: Two singers, as if two voices made twice the sound.
hint: Perceived loudness doubles for roughly every 10 decibels added.
steps: Perceived loudness doubles for about every 10 dB added.
Voices not in lockstep add their power.
reference: Stevens, The Measurement of Loudness, Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 1955
